mechanism: A fn/closure tail expression naming an owned local, param or field is not treated as a move: the value is dropped at scope exit and also returned.
Temporaries created in a fn's tail expression (incl. RefCell guards in a tail match scrutinee) are never dropped, nor are the locals.
A tail-position match that moves a by-value param/binding in some arms skips drops of the unmoved values/bindings.
Rust 2024 temporary scoping (block-tail temps dropped before locals, if-let scrutinee dropped before else) is not implemented.
Temporaries inside println!/format! arguments (and the enclosing statement) are dropped before the print instead of at end of statement.
A temporary used as a method receiver or place base (Box temp, T::mk(), const item PROTO.id) is never dropped.
A closure's by-value parameter is never dropped (expression-bodied closures, map/unwrap_or_else closures).
Calling a closure/fn-pointer with an aggregate by-value argument that is a field place or call result passes it wrongly (segfault / invalid free).
A format! String produced as the value of an if/match branch, closure return or similar expression position is never freed.
A closure returning a tuple returns a pointer to its own stack alloca.
`break <aggregate temporary/call>` from a loop loses the value and crashes.
A match expression that is the tail of a block used as a value (match arm, else block, closure body) is lowered with no/wrong value.
A nested fn item inside a block expression breaks the enclosing block's return lowering (llvm.return operand).
A closure whose body is a bare `unsafe { ...; }` block lowers a return with an operand.
Nested fn items are miscompiled when they take &dyn / slice params or call operator impls (wrong environment/ABI).
Struct-literal field is not a coercion site: Box<Concrete> is not unsized into a Box<dyn Trait> field, leaving a thin pointer.
A closure param that is a reference to a fat pointer (&Box<dyn>, &&dyn, &&[T]) is typed/loaded with one level of indirection too few.
Borrowing a closure literal directly at a call argument (&|x| .., &mut |v| ..) passes a dangling/uninitialised closure.
A move closure captures a reference to its source slot instead of copying, so returned/boxed closures read dangling or later-mutated captures.
An if-expression whose Box::new arms coerce to an annotated Box<dyn> computes garbage.
Match arms of different Box types are not unsized to the expected Box<dyn> type.
Unsize coercion Box<T>->Box<dyn> is not applied at vec! elements or nested generic ctor args (Rc::new(RefCell::new(Box::new..))); Box<dyn> is also rendered as &dyn.
vec![..] lowers to vec_from_arr<T: Copy>, refusing non-Copy elements unless the binding is annotated.
vec![x; n] with an annotated let or a runtime/assoc-const count does not parse or infer.
Structurally Copy types (Option<Copy>, auto-Copy structs, tuples with {integer}) and arrays/Option do not implement Copy/Clone as traits for bounds and derives.
A bare unit-variant/const path in a nested or ref-default-binding pattern (None, Some(K), tag: None) is resolved as a fresh binding.
The exhaustiveness check is skipped when the scrutinee is a reference (&Enum, default binding mode).
Matches over integers, chars, &str, slices, or structs with int/bool fields without a wildcard are never exhaustiveness-checked.
Range patterns inside a variant payload are not counted for exhaustiveness.
Slice patterns compute element offsets with the wrong stride for non-scalar elements and for positions after `..`.
Enum/tuple subpatterns nested inside a slice pattern (and slice patterns in let-else) leave their bindings undefined.
A literal/range/@-or subpattern under ref default binding mode compares the pointer without loading (MLIR type mismatch).
Refutable subpatterns (range in tuple, or-pattern with bindings) under a reference scrutinee match wrongly at runtime.
`for x in &vec` / slice over enum or Option elements iterates with the wrong element stride (.iter() is right).
By-value for over an array of 16-byte elements (&str, tuples, enums) reads garbage or segfaults.
Iterating an array of arrays yields element copies/garbage rows rather than references into the array.
Inside a const-generic context, [T; N] has length 0 at runtime (iter/len/iter_mut/range-slicing see no elements).
A const generic given only by turbofish (or via impl Trait return) has no value in the body at mono: reads 0 or ICE.
A const-generic struct literal without ::<N> inside impl<const N> resolves to Struct<error> and ICEs.
A const generic N is not inferred from an array argument/struct field ([T;3] vs [T;N]).
Const-generic arguments are not compared in type equality (V<3> accepted as V<2>).
A const item (or turbofish literal) as a const-generic argument is resolved as a type or mistyped.
In an array literal, later unsuffixed elements are not unified with the first element's type, giving mixed-width layouts.
const/static array or tuple initializers of unsuffixed literals ignore the declared element type and are stored as i32.
A literal aggregate or literal-initialised let passed behind & to an &i64/&[i64] site is built at i32 width.
&u8 is accepted where &i64 is expected (implicit widening through a reference), reading past the slot.
Implicit integer widening (u8->i64 etc.) is accepted across args, returns, branches and generics (untagged divergence).
Out-of-range integer literals in consts/operator RHS are accepted and truncated.
`u32 as char` (and i64 as char) casts are accepted.
The unsuffixed LHS literal of a shift is typed i32 regardless of the expected type, so `1 << 40` traps.
An int literal on the left of % with a u64 operand is typed signed.
Ranges default to RangeI32 ignoring suffixed bounds / expected type (usize ranges truncate).
An unsuffixed literal binding (or fold seed) is defaulted to i32 before later uses are seen.
The expected type (param, turbofish, closure param, field) does not reach unsuffixed literals inside generic/enum constructor args or closure returns.
A tail match gets no expected type from the fn return type.
A let annotation's element type flows into the receiver vec! literal of a method chain.
Loop break-value type is inferred from the first break (or a later return) and later breaks are lowered at the wrong type (None, i32 width).
`break None` is not unified with a sibling `break Some(x)`.
A tail let-chain if/else or loop with break values is not seen as covering all paths.
#[derive_partial_eq] on enums generates an eq that always returns true (REPEAT_GROUP over variants empty).
#[derive_debug] on enums prints only the type name.
derive(Debug) quotes a field name starting with 'c' as a c".." CStr literal.
The derive quote engine's REPEAT_GROUP fails for single-field structs, tuple structs and enums, so Clone/PartialEq/Ord generate nothing.
Derived/struct == on tuple or one-field structs lowers to an i32 condition (cf.cond_br verification failure).
derive_ord on an enum emits an unresolved `Self`.
Logos Eq declares its own eq, so PartialEq+Eq together make eq ambiguous (or a duplicate ne symbol).
Logos PartialOrd is a marker: derive(PartialOrd) provides no lt/partial_cmp.
An operator (==, >) on a generic instantiation dispatches to a method symbol (V2$G1$i64__eq, M__gt) that is never instantiated.
== on a generic struct instance is treated as moving its operands.
A trait static fn / assoc const / From called through a generic param is never emitted for the concrete impl (func.call to missing symbol).
derive(Copy)/impl Copy on a type with heap fields is accepted (no E0204), leading to double free.
Derives on a lifetime-generic struct emit an impl without the lifetime (E0726).
Derived impls are not visible inside impl-block method bodies (metaprog ordering).
derive_hash/derive_ord on raw-pointer fields fail in generated code.
Derives on const-generic structs treat N as a type param / are invisible in impl<const N>.
== on Vec/Option/Result/arrays and Vec::contains require Eq instead of PartialEq, or Vec has no eq at all.
== on a fieldless enum with no PartialEq impl is accepted as builtin.
Operators on enums ignore user Add/Sub/Neg impls and lower as integer arithmetic on the discriminant/pointer.
== on dyn Trait values is lowered as builtin (ignores impl PartialEq for dyn, accepted without impl).
Generic T is not inferred when the argument needs deref/unsize coercion (&Vec<T>->&[T], &Box<E<T>>->&E<T>).
sum()/collect() in return/tail position take no target type from the fn return type.
collect::<Vec<_>>() leaves `_` unresolved to codegen (Option<()>::replace no value).
A partially annotated `let v: Vec<_> = ..collect()` is refused.
Vec::new()'s element type is not inferred from a later &mut Vec<T> argument, param type or push.
for-in over a generic I: Iterator / impl Iterator param is refused, and generic adapters on it do not resolve.
Closure param/return types are not inferred from an expected Fn signature (impl Fn return, Box<dyn Fn>, &mut F).
Deref coercion (&&str->&str, &Box<T>->&T, &mut Box<T>->&mut T) is not applied at call args, assignments or if branches.
The |&x| closure param pattern does not strip the reference when the param type is inferred.
str::parse target from a let annotation/later use is not inferred and main is demoted to a trap stub.
`let n: i64 = s.parse()?` does not infer parse's F through `?`.
A generic F (or &F) passed straight into an iterator adapter / generic call cannot be inferred.
An untyped closure param inferred through a generic T (or generic compose/loop) leaves a TypeVar unresolved at mlir_gen.
Closure params whose types come from a generic bound fixed by sibling args are not inferred (&dyn Fn(A,T), Fn(&mut T)).
An untyped closure param inferred from a later direct call gives a void/garbage result.
Untyped closure params (mixed typed/untyped, generic tuple-struct ctor) crash the compiler.
An associated-type binding (S: Tr<A = i64>, Output = V) is not used to normalize the projection in the body.
An associated-type equality bound/RPIT binding is not checked at the call or return site.
Values of an associated-projection type (F::Out) are never dropped.
Moving a value of associated-projection type (field or *Box<M::Out>) is not tracked, so it is dropped twice.
A method call through &mut Box<dyn>/&mut [T;N] moves the reference instead of reborrowing.
Box/Rc/Ref inherent methods (unsafe get/get_mut, Ref::get) shadow the pointee's methods during the autoderef probe.
User methods/fns named like std items (count/last, pow) resolve to the std item.
Box<dyn Tr>::as_ref() resolves into the trait instead of Box.
A &mut method call through RefMut / vec[i] / generic RefCell is refused with an internal temp '_tN' behind &.
Tuple-field index .0 is not autoderef'd through Box/Rc/Ref.
`&None` / `&UnitStruct` resolves the path as a variable.
In a match on &Option, a bare None arm expression is typed as the scrutinee type.
`let r;` without type or initializer does not parse.
&impl Trait, impl A + B and impl Trait + 'a type syntax does not parse.
The `&'a self` receiver shorthand (and related ref/method-seam tokens) does not parse.
`impl Trait for (i64, i64)` does not parse.
A type-associated fn path used as a value (String::new, Type::method) is a syntax error or misresolved.
`for i in 0..` does not parse.
dyn Trait<Assoc = T> does not parse.
An untyped tuple-struct pattern closure param |Id(k)| does not parse.
A const item inside a fn body does not parse.
`<V<5> as Dim>::D` and generic unit structs do not parse.
Associated-type paths in expressions (D::Elem::default()) do not parse / mismatch.
A nested fn item can read locals of the enclosing fn (no E0434).
Nested fn items are not in scope in their own body/before declaration, and generic nested fns don't parse.
Range indexing requires a slice/array receiver (no Vec/String/&[T;N] deref), and &mut a[r] is typed &mut &[T].
str::split adapters (filter/map) demand 'a: 'static inside stdlib SplitPat.
An owning into_iter() wrapped in an adapter and consumed leaks the source buffer.
Box<dyn Trait> created by coercion (at generic args, in collections) gets drop glue that never runs the concrete Drop/field drops.
A generic struct passed by value to a generic param (incl. drop()) is never dropped.
Rc implements DerefMut in stdlib, so mutation through Rc is accepted.
A generic t: &T can call a &mut self trait method.
impl Trait return types leak the concrete type (fields, other traits, Copy, type identity).
A move closure owning non-Copy captures (impl FnOnce) is treated as Copy and can be used twice.
Rust 2024 RPIT capture of a &mut param lifetime is not enforced.
Generic bodies are checked only per instantiation, not against their bounds.
Raw-pointer derefs via &*p, (*p).method() on *const dyn, and autoderef method receivers escape the unsafe check.
A shared reference converts to *mut (by coercion or cast).
Moving an unsized dyn value out of a Box is accepted.
arr.len() after a partial move out of an array is accepted.
loop break values of different types are accepted.
A struct literal in match scrutinee position is accepted.
Vec<&T> built with iter().collect() does not carry the loan.
User Index/IndexMut operand is not type-checked against Idx.
Pushing Box<N> into Vec<Box<dyn Item>> without N: Item reaches codegen (no E0277).
Box<Box<dyn Trait>> construction/dispatch finds no vtable.
&dyn Trait from an unsuffixed literal leaves {integer} to vtable lookup.
&"lit" coerced to &dyn Display finds no vtable for &[u8].
{:?}/Display of containers of references (Option<&T>, Vec<&T>, &Box<String>) calls a fmt instance that is never emitted.
iter().max()/min().unwrap() over non-i32/i64 or user Ord elements resolves to an Option<&T>::unwrap instance that produces no value.
Iterator adapter chains (copied, Box<dyn Iterator>.map, bytes().take) resolve to adapter method instances that are never emitted or produce no value.
Methods of impl<T: PartialEq> / generic methods returning &'a T vanish at the call site (no value).
panic!() (and println!() in some programs) with no arguments crashes the metacall splice / is not diverging.
print! in a program with Box-containing user types fails in the metacall build (dealloc missing).
logosc segfaults on an infinite-size recursive struct instead of E0072.
logosc segfaults on an unclosed function-body brace.
Trait upcasting coercion is applied only at call-arg sites, not at let/return.
&*box_dyn inside println!/format! args is re-rendered without the deref (render-and-reparse), giving the &Box->&dyn E0277.
&**rb, &mut **rb, &*v[i] of Box<dyn> are typed as &Box<dyn> and refused as a cast.
Box<dyn>/&dyn default object lifetime is ignored (elision counts Box<dyn> as borrowed; returns borrow args).
Box<dyn Trait> is represented as &dyn internally, breaking generic Box<T: ?Sized>, impl for Box<dyn>, and -> Self in From.
&*p for *mut dyn is typed *mut dyn, and &mut *bx typed &dyn.
A closure returning a borrow of its reference param (or derived through a method) is refused by the region check.
Returning a reference through a &'a [T]/&'a dyn field or a slice-pattern binding is refused as escaping.
zip over generic slices then map reports a bogus 'parameter type may not live long enough'.
Array-literal temporaries in a for head and const array elements are not extended/promoted (dropped while borrowed).
A closure passing a captured &mut param into a call is refused as not declared mutable.
A closure only writing through a captured raw pointer is classified FnMut.
Match guards / refutable nested patterns inside a loop body lower bindings as re-assigned immutables ('cannot assign twice').
Nested/&/@ patterns inside enum-variant payloads (and let-else) are unsupported.
An array subpattern inside a struct field pattern is refused as refutable.
A `..` pattern over a partially moved struct is refused as use of moved value.
Destructuring with `..` after/instead of a partial move mis-tracks drops (whole marked moved, or moved field dropped again).
Struct update ..base in a fn tail/return does not drop overridden base fields.
Assignment through v[i] / IndexMut does not drop the overwritten element.
Vec::contains bit-copies non-Copy elements and drops the copy.
Vec swap/reverse on tuple elements corrupts or double-frees (element treated with wrong size/Copy).
Vec::truncate drops removed elements in reverse order.
Moving a heap-owning value out of a Box in a match arm is a use-after-free.
Moving the payload out of a Box (*b) leaks the box allocation.
A by-value method called through a Box field double-frees the moved contents.
match on *p for a *mut Enum fn parameter segfaults.
Conditional moves inside loops (move+continue, drop+break, moving the loop var) mis-set drop flags.
A closure body if that conditionally moves its by-value param emits an undefined drop flag.
A move closure returning its captured value by value drops the capture again.
A FnOnce move closure's captured String leaks when consumed by a generic.
Edition-2021 disjoint field capture is not implemented (move || n.id captures all of n).
Vec<Option<i64>> and Vec<Option<Box<J>>> share one instantiation/drop fn key.
A closure capturing a raw pointer loses the capture ('undefined base').
A by-value trait method called through &T on a Copy generic passes a pointer.
An unresolved {integer} in a tuple via break value or fold seed reaches codegen.
A const expression used directly as a println! argument reads uninitialised memory.
An enum implementing a trait with >=2 default methods fails on the second.
Box<T> has no Clone; .clone() resolves to T::clone.
&T does not implement Clone.
items[0].clone() on a user Clone type keeps items borrowed.
Box/Rc/Ref and std forwarding impls (Display/Debug etc.) are missing.
&[T] does not implement Debug.
Tuples do not implement Ord.
char Ord/Hash, Sum/Product for widths other than i32/i64 and similar core impls are missing.
Inherent methods on narrow ints / through references to primitives are missing (receiver not a struct).
RangeFrom used as an iterator yields nothing.
stdlib Iterator is not object-safe (filter returns Self without Self: Sized).
str methods are not reachable from a String receiver through autoderef.
as_ptr on arrays/slices is refused or typed *const u8.
Option/Result combinators take fn pointers, refusing capturing closures.
HashMap::iter yields ZipPair instead of tuples.
RefCell::replace with non-Copy T fails to compile inside stdlib.
A custom Iterator with Item = Box<dyn> makes stdlib default methods fail borrow check.
RangeInclusive<u8>::contains returns false for values in range.
char::is_alphabetic etc. are ASCII-only.
u16 multiplication overflow wraps silently.
{:e} float formatting differs from Rust.
VecIter::find on an iterator over a &Vec param reports a variance mismatch.
Blanket impls (generic supertrait impl, impl<F: FnMut> for F, tuple impls) are not found when checking a bound.
A default trait method calling Self::static_fn fails for a generic impl.
Box<dyn Fn> does not satisfy an impl Fn / F: Fn bound.
? and .into() in a generic fn ignore an E: From<X> bound.
A method-level generic param drops the impl's T: Copy bound.
impl Trait nested inside another type (Option<impl>, Box<impl> arg) is refused / not inferred.
A recursive -> impl Trait fn with a concrete base case is refused.
Operator impls for &T (impl Mul<i64> for &T, impl Neg for &P) are not dispatched.
Binary operators are not dispatched to a generic impl<T> Add for M<T> (the method call works).
An impl method with an elided lifetime does not match the trait's &'a param.
impl Mul for V next to impl Mul<i64> for V is refused as duplicate Output.
`+=` on a user type calls Add instead of AddAssign (and is accepted with only Add).
The closure's second param in .copied().fold stays generic T / the operator operand is not inferred.
An associated const typed Self / Self::Val cannot be implemented.
An associated const referring to a const generic param is an undefined variable.
A nested tuple pattern through a reference binds the pointer instead of the field.
A method call on an iter_mut() item of Vec<enum> fails 'receiver is not a struct'.
collect/sum into Result<Vec>/Option<Vec> is unsupported; Result::ok as a fn path fails.
A local item whose name matches a private/imported std item is refused or mixed up.
A match arm `{ expr; }` is typed as expr's type, not ().
A closure body that is an if without else is refused as an expression.
A unit variant nested inside Box::new in a generic enum ctor gets no T from the enclosing variant.
? inside a closure without an annotated return type is attributed to the enclosing fn.
Trait static calls with Self inferred from context (Default::default(), Make::make) are refused.
Generic struct update syntax does not infer type args from the base (refused or Struct<error> ICE).
An empty array literal with turbofish into a slice param produces invalid MLIR.
A primitive method path (i32::max) as a fold fn is an undefined symbol.
A recursive generic enum with two methods and two instantiations gets duplicate mangled bodies.
The compiler hangs on a generic BST insert over Option<Box<Tree<K,V>>>.
A generic-enum method whose signature does not mention T cannot be inferred inside another generic fn.
[first, ..] over a &mut slice binds first as & instead of &mut.
null_mut() is not inferred for a generic struct field *mut T.
A break-value expression reading a field/loop local (b.val, s.len(), format!) marks the operand moved.
A match guard using a binding nested in a variant/tuple-struct subpattern refers to an undefined value and crashes logosc.
An `as *mut _` placeholder is not inferred from later uses.
Reassigning a &Box<dyn> binding double-frees the Vec element.
A generic struct literal field set from Vec::new() or an array needing unsizing does not infer T.

A move closure using self.field through &self tries to move self.
Calling an impl Fn(T)->T returned by a generic struct method yields void.
